title: An Evaluation of Zero-Shot Classification of Multimodal Foundation Models for Point Clouds
content: Modelling the existing building stock for maintenance, renovation, and decommissioning relies on point clouds from laser scanning or photogrammetry, whose objects must be segmented and classified, traditionally with computer vision models that require task-specific training. To avoid this training, this paper proposes to use the zero-shot classification capabilities of multimodal foundation models (MMFMs) for the pre-classification of segmented point clouds. Our approach renders one to four isometric views of each object and classifies them with MMFMs. Weevaluate it on the public datasets ModelNet40 and S3DIS Area 5 across several MMFMs. OnModelNet40, the best configuration, Gemini-3.6-Flash with four views, achieves 55.4% accuracy and a Macro-F1 of 47.7%, and all six MMFMs evaluated with one to four views improve as the number of views increases. On S3DIS, adding textual dimensions derived from an axis-aligned bounding box (AABB) to the RGB views improves the accuracy of all four evaluated models; for Gemini-3.6-Flash, accuracy increases from 42.1% to 60.5% with a Macro-F1 of 59.7%. While MMFMs remain below specialised trained classifiers, they show that MMFMs can support the zero-shot pre-classification of segmented point clouds and could support bootstrapping the annotation of training data. The evaluation framework is publicly available on GitHub.
